question: Which of the following is listed in the manual as one of the basic control skills exercises you may be tested on?
explanation: The manual lists straight line backing, offset back/right, offset back/left, parallel park (driver side), parallel park (conventional), and alley dock as the basic control skills exercises.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, p. 12-1

question: During basic control skills testing, what does the manual define as an 'encroachment'?
choice_a: Failing to complete the exercise within a time limit
choice_b: Touching or crossing over an exercise boundary line or cone with any portion of your vehicle
choice_c: Asking the examiner for extra instructions
explanation: The manual states the examiner scores encroachments as the number of times you touch or cross over an exercise boundary line or cone with any portion of your vehicle, and each encroachment counts as an error.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, p. 12-1

question: Per the manual, what is a 'pull-up' during a basic control skills exercise?
choice_a: Stopping the vehicle and pulling forward to clear an encroachment or get a better position
choice_b: Any time the vehicle comes to a stop without changing direction
choice_c: Pulling the parking brake before exiting the vehicle
choice_d: Pulling the vehicle into its final parked position
explanation: The manual states that when a driver stops and pulls forward to clear an encroachment or to get a better position, it is scored as a 'pull-up'; stopping without changing direction does not count as a pull-up.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, p. 12-1

question: What does the manual say about how pull-ups are scored?
choice_a: Any single pull-up results in automatic failure of the exercise
choice_b: Pull-ups are never counted as errors
choice_c: Only the last pull-up in an exercise counts as an error
choice_d: You will not be penalized for initial pull-ups, but an excessive number of pull-ups will count as errors
explanation: The manual states you will not be penalized for initial pull-ups; however, an excessive number of pull-ups will count as errors.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, p. 12-1

question: Before exiting the vehicle to perform an outside vehicle observation ('look'), what must you do?
choice_b: Place the vehicle in neutral and set the parking brake(s)
choice_c: Sound the horn to alert the examiner
choice_d: Roll down all of the vehicle's windows
explanation: The manual states that when safely stopping and exiting to check the external position of the vehicle, you must place the vehicle in neutral and set the parking brake(s).
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, p. 12-1

question: What is the maximum number of 'looks' (outside vehicle observations) permitted for most basic control skills exercises, and how many are allowed specifically for the Straight Line Backing exercise?
choice_a: Three for most exercises; two for Straight Line Backing
choice_b: Unlimited looks are allowed for all exercises
choice_c: Two for most exercises; one for Straight Line Backing
choice_d: One for most exercises; two for Straight Line Backing
explanation: The manual states the maximum number of times you may look to check the position of your vehicle is two, except for the Straight Line Backing exercise, which allows one look.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, p. 12-1

question: When safely exiting the vehicle (non-bus) to check its external position, what must the driver do?
choice_a: Face the vehicle and maintain three points of contact with it at all times
choice_b: Exit as quickly as possible to save time
choice_c: Exit facing away from the vehicle to watch for traffic
choice_d: Maintain only two points of contact with the vehicle
explanation: The manual requires exiting the vehicle safely by facing the vehicle and maintaining three points of contact with the vehicle at all times.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, p. 12-1

question: In the Alley Dock exercise, how close must the rear of your vehicle come to the rear of the alley?
explanation: The manual instructs that you must back into the alley bringing the rear of your vehicle within three feet of the rear of the alley without touching boundary lines or cones.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, p. 12-2

question: What does the manual require regarding the Parallel Park (Conventional) exercise?
choice_a: Only the rear half of the vehicle needs to be in the parking space
choice_b: You are required to get your entire vehicle completely into the space
choice_c: The vehicle may cross the front boundary marked by cones
choice_d: The exercise requires parking on the left side of the road
explanation: The manual states that for the conventional parallel park (space on your right), you are required to get your entire vehicle completely into the space without crossing front, side, or rear boundaries marked by cones.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, p. 12-2

question: According to the manual, what must you do at all times during the on-road driving test?
choice_a: Maintain a following distance of at least one vehicle length
choice_b: Signal all lane changes and turns exactly 100 feet in advance
choice_c: Wear your safety belt, obey all traffic signs, signals, and laws, and complete the test without an accident or moving violation
explanation: The manual states that at all times during the test you must drive in a safe and responsible manner, wear your safety belt, obey all traffic signs, signals, and laws, and complete the test without an accident or moving violation.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 13 - On-Road Driving, p. 13-1

question: According to the manual, what is 'unsafe coasting' while approaching a turn?
choice_a: Having the vehicle out of gear (clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral) for more than the length of your vehicle
choice_b: Braking too early before the turn
choice_c: Signaling more than 100 feet before the turn
choice_d: Turning the steering wheel before the vehicle begins to move
explanation: The manual defines unsafe coasting as occurring when your vehicle is out of gear (clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral) for more than the length of your vehicle.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 13 - On-Road Driving, p. 13-1

question: If you must stop behind another vehicle before making a turn, where should you stop?
choice_a: As close as possible to the vehicle ahead
choice_b: At least two car lengths behind the vehicle ahead
choice_d: Where you can see the rear tires of the vehicle ahead of you
explanation: The manual states that if stopping behind another vehicle, you should stop where you can see the rear tires on the vehicle ahead of you, maintaining a safe gap.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 13 - On-Road Driving, p. 13-1

question: For buses, school buses, or vehicles displaying placards, within what distance of the nearest rail must the vehicle stop at a railroad crossing?
choice_a: Within 100 feet but not less than 25 feet
choice_b: Within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet
choice_c: Within 25 feet but not less than 5 feet
explanation: The manual states these vehicles should stop within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail at every railroad crossing (unless the crossing is exempt).
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 13 - On-Road Driving, p. 13-3

question: According to the manual's clutch usage guidance for manual transmissions, what must a driver do if the vehicle has an unsynchronized manual transmission?
choice_a: Avoid using the clutch except when starting the vehicle
choice_b: Ride the clutch to control speed
choice_d: Coast with the clutch depressed between shifts
explanation: The manual states that if equipped with an unsynchronized manual transmission, you must double-clutch when shifting, and you should not rev or lug the engine.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 13 - On-Road Driving, p. 13-3

question: Under the manual's Lane Usage guidance for general driving behaviors, where should you finish a right turn?
choice_b: In the lane closest to the center line
explanation: The manual states you should finish a right turn in the right-most (curb) lane.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 13 - On-Road Driving, p. 13-4
